reason: Combine the cold cloud with the surviving knot to follow whether its clumps can form stars.
expectation: The added cold gas may help the knot collapse into a new generation of stars, though it might first form an intermediate gathering.

alternatives.reason: This could follow dust carried by the outflow, but I want to pursue the surviving clumps first.

effect: The surviving clumps formed young stars, completing that goal; I can now follow the dust.
reaction: It's satisfying to see material from the old pillars become stars in a new location.
reason: Follow the dusty gas carried by the nursery outflow, one of the two paths described in the introduction.
expectation: The outflow will carry some dust away from the nursery, perhaps toward the outer galaxy.

alternatives.reason: The dust remaining near the young stars is also relevant, but I want to follow the outflow first.

effect: The outflow has carried dust outward; it can now be followed into the galaxy's outer gas.
reaction: The result matches the expected dust transport, though it gives little detail yet.
reason: Follow the carried dust into the hot outer gas to see what happens to it.
expectation: The dust may disperse or be altered by the hot outer gas; its fate is uncertain.

alternatives.reason: This follows the other dust path near the stars, but I want to finish tracing the outward dust first.

effect: Hot outer gas erodes many dust grains, so I'll follow the remaining path near the young stars.
reaction: The return of grain material to the gas is an interesting contrast with dust surviving in the disk.
reason: This is the only offered combination and follows the other dust path described in the chapter.
expectation: The young stars may warm the nearby dust, though I don't know exactly what will result.

effect: The remaining dust absorbs starlight and radiates in infrared, completing the dust goal and the chapter.
reaction: The distinction between glowing gas and warm grains was a useful closing detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the surviving pillar clumps into new stars was most satisfying: it gave their earlier survival a meaningful consequence.

leastWorthwhile.text: Carrying dust outward was the least engaging passage on its own; the result gave little detail until the next step.

surprise.text: I was interested that hot outer gas erodes dust grains and returns their material to the gas, rather than merely dispersing them.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: both dust paths were introduced in the chapter, though the last combination was the only offered action.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the material's different histories connect, particularly after the clumps formed stars and the dust followed contrasting paths.
